cards.f: Q3 extended response: marks and length?
cards.b: 25 marks (15 reading + 10 writing). 250-350 words, about 35 minutes.
Letter, report, journal, speech, interview or article.
Go beyond what the text states: explain why, imagine consequences, link details, always grounded in the text.
Many ideas from text, developed with convincing inferences, stays in role, all bullets covered.
Retells the text, little inference, bullets missing, may copy.
Voice and register, clear paragraph structure, own words, varied vocabulary and sentences, accuracy.
Greeting (Dear...), purpose in first paragraph, sign-off matching register.
First person, mixed tenses, reflective, honest feelings.
Address audience, direct appeals, rhetorical questions, memorable ending.
Title, formal tone, perhaps subheadings, objective, recommendations at end.
Question-and-answer layout with names; developed answers in voice.
Headline, engaging opening, aimed at readers.
5 min label details to bullets, 5 min plan, 22 min write, 3 min check.

cards.f: Which bullet usually needs most development?
cards.b: Bullet 3, usually opinion or prediction needing development.
Do not add events unsupported by the text (e.g. a secret love affair).

gaps.s: To go beyond what the text states while staying grounded in it is to ___ ideas.
A private, reflective form written in first person is a ___ entry.
A formal, objective form with a title and recommendations is a ___.
Staying in the character you are given is staying in ___.
A speech should include rhetorical ___ to engage listeners.
In Q3 you must not ___ from Text C but use your own words.

short.model: Develop means going beyond the text by explaining why, imagining consequences or giving reactions, while staying grounded in the text.

short.q: State two conventions of a speech. [2]
short.model: Address the audience directly and use rhetorical questions or direct appeals; end memorably.

short.q: State two errors that cap a Q3 answer at low reading levels. [2]
short.model: Retelling the text in order and copying phrases from it.

short.q: Plan how to use the 35 minutes. [4]
short.model: 5 minutes labelling details, 5 planning, 22 writing about 300 words, 3 checking.
It usually needs inference and development, which carry the most reading marks. One sentence is too little.
